Description: Zubrowka Province is the geographical area where the Commissioner of Police operates and where M. Gustave H is arrested.

[M. GUSTAVE H]
Description: M. Gustave H is a main character who dictates a will making Zero his sole heir, is arrested for the murder of Madame Céline Villeneuve Desgoffe und Taxis, and is later imprisoned at Check-point 19 Criminal Internment Camp where he beats Pinky Bandinski.

[M. GUSTAVE]
Description: M. Gustave is a central and complex character, primarily known as the meticulous, liberally perfumed, and charming head concierge of the Grand Budapest Hotel in Nebelsbad. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

His life takes a dramatic turn following Madame D.'s death, which deeply affects him. He becomes embroiled in a dispute over her will, specifically concerning the valuable "Boy with Apple" painting, which he is bequeathed and later becomes the current owner of. Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

During his ordeal, M. Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. He is seen distributing food, including Mendl's pastries, to convicts, earning their trust as a "straight fella." After escaping with Zero's assistance, he is left without a safe house and plans to use disguises, aiming to escape to the Maltese Riviera and retrieve the "Boy with Apple."

M. Gustave is eventually cleared of the murder charges, having an alibi involving the Duke of Westfalia's wife. He continues his adventures with Zero, discovering a strangled person, chasing Jopling on a sled, and being saved by Zero from Jopling's attempts to leave him dangling from a cliff. He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

Later, M. Gustave expresses profound disgust and sadness over the transformation of the Grand Budapest Hotel into a "troop's barracks." He interviews Agatha, flirts with her, and approves of her union with Zero. Ultimately, M. Gustave anoints Zero as his successor as concierge. Though initially detained, he is released by Henckels. However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. He is remembered as a refined hotelier, a philosophical and nihilistic character, and a man deeply moved by a pastry from Mendl's.

=== ENTITIES ===

[ZERO]
Description: "ZERO" is introduced as a Junior Lobby Boy in training at the Grand Budapest Hotel, who quickly becomes the devoted pupil, counselor, and guardian of M. Gustave. He is later known as Mr. Moustafa, and ultimately becomes M. Gustave's sole heir and successor at the Grand Budapest Hotel, also serving as the narrator (Mr. Moustafa V.O.).

Zero is a refugee from Aq Salim al-Jabat, having fled a war that destroyed his family and village, rendering him stateless and requiring a Special Transit Permit and a Migratory Visa with Stage Three Worker Status. He is deeply in love with Agatha, his girlfriend, to whom he proposes marriage and gives a book. He is protective and jealous of her, and works at Mendl's, often driving their delivery truck and carrying pastry boxes.

Throughout his adventures, Zero acts as M. Gustave's personal valet, accomplice, protégé, and trusted companion. He accompanies M. Gustave on numerous journeys and escapades, observing events, following instructions from monks, and assisting with various tasks, from navigating churches to preparing for travel. He is sworn to secrecy about The Society of the Crossed Keys. Zero plays a crucial role in the theft of the "Boy with Apple" painting, agreeing to a blood-pact with M. Gustave to sell it. He is instrumental in saving M. Gustave from Jopling, helping him escape Henckels' troops, and suggesting their escape plan to the Maltese Riviera.

Zero discovers Serge's murdered body, chases Jopling on a sled with M. Gustave, and retaliates against Dmitri when M. Gustave is attacked. He is arrested and injured during M. Gustave's detention but is later released by Henckels. He is questioned by authorities and visits M. Gustave in prison. Zero is also depicted as agile, capable of shimmying up skylights and running across roofs to communicate with Agatha. He is concerned for M. Gustave, discussing his legal situation and bringing him treats.

As Mr. Moustafa, he trains the new Lobby Boy, Otto, and expresses alarm and shared sentiments about the hotel's declining state. He is a trusted staff member who reads M. Gustave's letters to the assembled staff. Zero's journey culminates in him finding and embracing Agatha, solidifying his personal happiness before his eventual succession to M. Gustave's legacy.

[CONCIERGE DESK]
Description: A specific station located in the Lobby of the Grand Budapest Hotel where Zero is seen substituting.

[GENERAL VON SHRECKER]
Description: An individual of authority who made a personal request to M. Chuck regarding hotel arrangements.

[M. CHUCK]
Description: M. Chuck is an officer who holds the position of Military Concierge at the Grand Budapest Hotel. In this role, he is responsible for dictating orders, managing guest requests, and overseeing guest services. He greeted Mr. Desgoffe und Taxis (also referred to as Dmitri) and his sisters upon their arrival, assisting them with booking their suite. M. Chuck was also tasked by General von Shrecker to ensure a specific matter. Beyond his concierge duties, he was involved in an investigation and later worked as staff under Zero at the Grand Budapest Hotel. Additionally, M. Chuck was a character who accompanied Henckels during a shootout.

[M. JEAN]
Description: M. Jean was a concierge at the Grand Budapest Hotel, described as West-continental in origin. He possessed a crooked nose and was known for being both lazy and accommodating. M. Jean was observed smoking cigarettes and interacted directly with the Author. His duties included assisting a fat businessman, and his capabilities were later a topic of discussion between the Author and Mr. Moustafa. Notably, M. Jean eventually abandoned his post at the hotel.

[GRAND BUDAPEST]
Description: The Grand Budapest is a central hotel establishment and institution that serves as the primary setting for the story's events. It is owned by Mr. Moustafa.

Historically, The Grand Budapest was a prestigious hotel renowned for its high and impeccable standards. M. Gustave was deeply associated with the establishment, serving as its beloved, original concierge and carrying its pass-keys. He was a staunch upholder of its reputation, entrusting it to the staff during his incarceration and apologizing on its behalf to Zero. Both M. Gustave and Zero previously worked at the hotel, implied to have served as Lobby Boys.

However, The Grand Budapest experienced a significant decline over time. It is described in a later state as nearly-empty, featuring faded couches, fraying armchairs, and threadbare carpets. Furthermore, it was transformed into a "troop's barracks," a change that caused M. Gustave great distress. Despite its eventual state of disrepair, The Grand Budapest remains the pivotal setting for the narrative.

=== ENTITIES ===

[SERGE]
Description: Serge is a character who served in a butler-like capacity at the location where M. Gustave and Zero were present. He assisted them with various tasks, including helping to wrap the "Boy with Apple" painting, during which he appeared distressed, and aiding M. Gustave in the kitchen. Despite these interactions, M. Gustave held a negative view of Serge, describing him as a "frightened, little, yellow-bellied coward" and expressing anger towards him, as Serge had previously betrayed him.

Serge played a crucial role in the events surrounding Madame D's will and M. Gustave's murder case. He was an aged individual and an official witness to Madame D's second will. He became a key witness in M. Gustave's murder case, having ostensibly seen the alleged events. Serge revealed critical information to M. Gustave before his death.

His personal life was marked by tragedy, as his family was murdered, and he is implied to be the brother of a sister whose severed head was found. Serge attempted to evade authorities by fleeing the jurisdiction after becoming a witness, but he was ultimately found. He was killed violently during the conduct of his duties, found strangled. M. Gustave and Zero observed a moment of silence for him following his death.

[CONFESSIONAL BOOTH]
Description: A dark, wooden box lined with purple velvet located in the transept of the church, used for confession, where M. Gustave, Zero, and Serge meet.

[M. GUSTAVE]
Description: M. Gustave is a central and complex character, primarily known as the meticulous, liberally perfumed, and charming head concierge of the Grand Budapest Hotel in Nebelsbad. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

His life takes a dramatic turn following Madame D.'s death, which deeply affects him. He becomes embroiled in a dispute over her will, specifically concerning the valuable "Boy with Apple" painting, which he is bequeathed and later becomes the current owner of. Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

During his ordeal, M. Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. He is seen distributing food, including Mendl's pastries, to convicts, earning their trust as a "straight fella." After escaping with Zero's assistance, he is left without a safe house and plans to use disguises, aiming to escape to the Maltese Riviera and retrieve the "Boy with Apple."

M. Gustave is eventually cleared of the murder charges, having an alibi involving the Duke of Westfalia's wife. He continues his adventures with Zero, discovering a strangled person, chasing Jopling on a sled, and being saved by Zero from Jopling's attempts to leave him dangling from a cliff. He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

Later, M. Gustave expresses profound disgust and sadness over the transformation of the Grand Budapest Hotel into a "troop's barracks." He interviews Agatha, flirts with her, and approves of her union with Zero. Ultimately, M. Gustave anoints Zero as his successor as concierge. Though initially detained, he is released by Henckels. However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. He is remembered as a refined hotelier, a philosophical and nihilistic character, and a man deeply moved by a pastry from Mendl's.

[M. SERGE]
Description: A butler described as anxious, distraught, exhausted, and terrified, who requested a private word with M. Gustave and is observed by Mr. Moustafa.

[BUTLER'S PANTRY]
Description: A small room adjacent to the kitchen in Dmitri's home, where Serge guides M. Gustave and Zero.

results.context_text:
=== ENTITIES ===

[M. GUSTAVE]
Description: M. Gustave is a central and complex character, primarily known as the meticulous, liberally perfumed, and charming head concierge of the Grand Budapest Hotel in Nebelsbad. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

His life takes a dramatic turn following Madame D.'s death, which deeply affects him. He becomes embroiled in a dispute over her will, specifically concerning the valuable "Boy with Apple" painting, which he is bequeathed and later becomes the current owner of. Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

During his ordeal, M. Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. He is seen distributing food, including Mendl's pastries, to convicts, earning their trust as a "straight fella." After escaping with Zero's assistance, he is left without a safe house and plans to use disguises, aiming to escape to the Maltese Riviera and retrieve the "Boy with Apple."

M. Gustave is eventually cleared of the murder charges, having an alibi involving the Duke of Westfalia's wife. He continues his adventures with Zero, discovering a strangled person, chasing Jopling on a sled, and being saved by Zero from Jopling's attempts to leave him dangling from a cliff. He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

Later, M. Gustave expresses profound disgust and sadness over the transformation of the Grand Budapest Hotel into a "troop's barracks." He interviews Agatha, flirts with her, and approves of her union with Zero. Ultimately, M. Gustave anoints Zero as his successor as concierge. Though initially detained, he is released by Henckels. However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. He is remembered as a refined hotelier, a philosophical and nihilistic character, and a man deeply moved by a pastry from Mendl's.

Description: An important business asset bequeathed to M. Gustave in the will.

Description: A specific suite in the hotel where M. Gustave is staying.

[HOTEL TRADE]
Description: The industry sector that M. Gustave believes will experience a long dry-spell due to the "war" and "troubles".

results.context_text:
=== ENTITIES ===

[AGATHA]
Description: Agatha is a central character, introduced as Zero's girlfriend and later his wife, for whom Zero (Mr. Moustafa) keeps the Grand Budapest Hotel, wearing her crossed-keys pendant as a symbol of their connection. Zero deeply loves her, proposes marriage, and credits her with having "saved them." M. Gustave also admires Agatha for her purity.

Agatha is a seventeen-year-old girl with distinctive freckles and a birthmark. She works at Mendl's pâtisserie as a highly skilled pastry chef, known for her expertise with a palette knife and butter-cream flourish, making and delivering beautifully-decorated pastries from Herr Mendl to the Executive Staff. She is described as cautious, observant, and brave, though she can be frightened, such as during an arrest by soldiers while traveling with M. Gustave and Zero. She is also depicted reading romantic poetry.

Her role in the unfolding events is crucial. Agatha is informed about the stolen "Boy with Apple" painting and given a coded message for her survival. She is seen running away, carrying a wrapped painting, and is pursued by Dmitri Desgoffe und Taxis through the hotel lobby and into an elevator, while simultaneously being sought by M. Gustave and Zero. During her efforts, she attempts to escape through a skylight from a building in a sleeping village, interacts with a soldier, finds a brass key, unlocks a vault, and retrieves the wrapped painting, noticing a detail on its back. She falls with Zero into a Mendl's van during their escape and receives a sliver of paper from him.

=== ENTITIES ===

[DEPUTY KOVACS]
Description: Deputy Kovacs is a multifaceted individual who serves as both a deputy and an important attorney. In his legal capacity, he is the executor of Madame D.'s estate, obligated to the rule of law, and represents the deceased in inheritance matters. He operates from an art-deco office where he discusses Madame D's will and a crucial missing document. He is also responsible for presiding over and reading Madame D's Last Will and Testament to an audience.

As a deputy, Kovacs is involved in investigating M. Gustave's case, secretly meeting with Zero, and harbors suspicions regarding M. Gustave's innocence. His activities include emerging from an office building, taking a tram, and following Jopling to the Kunstmuseum Lutz. His office also postponed a meeting with Herr Becker.

Tragically, Deputy Kovacs was attacked by Jopling at the Kunstmuseum Lutz, an assault that resulted in his fingers being severed. He was subsequently reported missing and ultimately killed, with Dmitri Desgoffe und Taxis accused of his murder. Additionally, Deputy Kovacs is described as an emissary for the unknown owner of the Grand Budapest Hotel, making monthly visits to review books, convey messages, and meet with M. Gustave and Herr Becker.

[MR. MOUSTAFA]
Description: Mr. Moustafa is the elderly, smartly dressed, white-haired seventy-year-old man who is the current owner and proprietor of the Grand Budapest Hotel. He is revealed to be the older Zero, the future identity of Zero Moustafa, who once served as a Junior Lobby Boy under M. Gustave H. at the same hotel. Having formerly been the richest man in Zubrowka, he acquired the Grand Budapest Hotel through negotiation with the new government and maintains it for Agatha, whom he deeply loved and becomes distressed when speaking of her. He is described as a lonely figure.

Mr. Moustafa serves as the primary narrator of the story, providing extensive voice-over commentary on past events. He initiates a conversation with the Author in the spa, inviting him to dinner to recount his life story, particularly focusing on M. Gustave, the original concierge. He describes M. Gustave's character, the women he consorted with, and is implied to have inherited M. Gustave's possessions.

As a narrator, he offers detailed contextual information, including the intricacies of a conspiracy involving the powerful Desgoffe und Taxis family, his observations of Serge, and the broader unfolding situation. He also provides historical context regarding the war, detailing events such as the fall of Pffeifelstad, the surge of the Zig-zags, the Lutz Blitz, and High-command's advance to Nebelsbad. His narration also covers specific incidents like Herr Becker receiving a peculiar notice from Deputy Kovacs' office and his own meeting with Agatha. He works long hours at the hotel, diligently preserving its legacy.

[ZERO]
Description: "ZERO" is introduced as a Junior Lobby Boy in training at the Grand Budapest Hotel, who quickly becomes the devoted pupil, counselor, and guardian of M. Gustave. He is later known as Mr. Moustafa, and ultimately becomes M. Gustave's sole heir and successor at the Grand Budapest Hotel, also serving as the narrator (Mr. Moustafa V.O.).

Zero is a refugee from Aq Salim al-Jabat, having fled a war that destroyed his family and village, rendering him stateless and requiring a Special Transit Permit and a Migratory Visa with Stage Three Worker Status. He is deeply in love with Agatha, his girlfriend, to whom he proposes marriage and gives a book. He is protective and jealous of her, and works at Mendl's, often driving their delivery truck and carrying pastry boxes.

Throughout his adventures, Zero acts as M. Gustave's personal valet, accomplice, protégé, and trusted companion. He accompanies M. Gustave on numerous journeys and escapades, observing events, following instructions from monks, and assisting with various tasks, from navigating churches to preparing for travel. He is sworn to secrecy about The Society of the Crossed Keys. Zero plays a crucial role in the theft of the "Boy with Apple" painting, agreeing to a blood-pact with M. Gustave to sell it. He is instrumental in saving M. Gustave from Jopling, helping him escape Henckels' troops, and suggesting their escape plan to the Maltese Riviera.

Zero discovers Serge's murdered body, chases Jopling on a sled with M. Gustave, and retaliates against Dmitri when M. Gustave is attacked. He is arrested and injured during M. Gustave's detention but is later released by Henckels. He is questioned by authorities and visits M. Gustave in prison. Zero is also depicted as agile, capable of shimmying up skylights and running across roofs to communicate with Agatha. He is concerned for M. Gustave, discussing his legal situation and bringing him treats.

As Mr. Moustafa, he trains the new Lobby Boy, Otto, and expresses alarm and shared sentiments about the hotel's declining state. He is a trusted staff member who reads M. Gustave's letters to the assembled staff. Zero's journey culminates in him finding and embracing Agatha, solidifying his personal happiness before his eventual succession to M. Gustave's legacy.

[AGATHA]
Description: Agatha is a central character, introduced as Zero's girlfriend and later his wife, for whom Zero (Mr. Moustafa) keeps the Grand Budapest Hotel, wearing her crossed-keys pendant as a symbol of their connection. Zero deeply loves her, proposes marriage, and credits her with having "saved them." M. Gustave also admires Agatha for her purity.

Agatha is a seventeen-year-old girl with distinctive freckles and a birthmark. She works at Mendl's pâtisserie as a highly skilled pastry chef, known for her expertise with a palette knife and butter-cream flourish, making and delivering beautifully-decorated pastries from Herr Mendl to the Executive Staff. She is described as cautious, observant, and brave, though she can be frightened, such as during an arrest by soldiers while traveling with M. Gustave and Zero. She is also depicted reading romantic poetry.

Her role in the unfolding events is crucial. Agatha is informed about the stolen "Boy with Apple" painting and given a coded message for her survival. She is seen running away, carrying a wrapped painting, and is pursued by Dmitri Desgoffe und Taxis through the hotel lobby and into an elevator, while simultaneously being sought by M. Gustave and Zero. During her efforts, she attempts to escape through a skylight from a building in a sleeping village, interacts with a soldier, finds a brass key, unlocks a vault, and retrieves the wrapped painting, noticing a detail on its back. She falls with Zero into a Mendl's van during their escape and receives a sliver of paper from him.

Tragically, Agatha is later killed by the Prussian grippe, along with her infant son.

[HOTEL]
Description: An establishment, specifically its lobby, that is bustling with military personnel (implied Zig-zags) during the war.

[GRAND BUDAPEST]
Description: The Grand Budapest is a central hotel establishment and institution that serves as the primary setting for the story's events. It is owned by Mr. Moustafa.

Historically, The Grand Budapest was a prestigious hotel renowned for its high and impeccable standards. M. Gustave was deeply associated with the establishment, serving as its beloved, original concierge and carrying its pass-keys. He was a staunch upholder of its reputation, entrusting it to the staff during his incarceration and apologizing on its behalf to Zero. Both M. Gustave and Zero previously worked at the hotel, implied to have served as Lobby Boys.

However, The Grand Budapest experienced a significant decline over time. It is described in a later state as nearly-empty, featuring faded couches, fraying armchairs, and threadbare carpets. Furthermore, it was transformed into a "troop's barracks," a change that caused M. Gustave great distress. Despite its eventual state of disrepair, The Grand Budapest remains the pivotal setting for the narrative.

[HERR MENDL]
Description: Herr Mendl is a heavy-set baker who works at Mendl's pâtisserie. He is responsible for checking on various pastries, including gateaux l'Opéra. Herr Mendl is the individual who provides the renowned pastries, such as the Courtesan au chocolat and other "compliments," which Agatha delivers to the Executive Staff. His establishment is also the source from which M. Gustave and Zero obtain complimentary pastry boxes. Beyond his professional duties, Herr Mendl is depicted as a character who looks into Agatha's bedroom, instructing her to go to sleep, specifically after Zero escapes through the skylight.

[M. GUSTAVE]
Description: M. Gustave is a central and complex character, primarily known as the meticulous, liberally perfumed, and charming head concierge of the Grand Budapest Hotel in Nebelsbad. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

His life takes a dramatic turn following Madame D.'s death, which deeply affects him. He becomes embroiled in a dispute over her will, specifically concerning the valuable "Boy with Apple" painting, which he is bequeathed and later becomes the current owner of. Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

During his ordeal, M. Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. He is seen distributing food, including Mendl's pastries, to convicts, earning their trust as a "straight fella." After escaping with Zero's assistance, he is left without a safe house and plans to use disguises, aiming to escape to the Maltese Riviera and retrieve the "Boy with Apple."

M. Gustave is eventually cleared of the murder charges, having an alibi involving the Duke of Westfalia's wife. He continues his adventures with Zero, discovering a strangled person, chasing Jopling on a sled, and being saved by Zero from Jopling's attempts to leave him dangling from a cliff. He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

Later, M. Gustave expresses profound disgust and sadness over the transformation of the Grand Budapest Hotel into a "troop's barracks." He interviews Agatha, flirts with her, and approves of her union with Zero. Ultimately, M. Gustave anoints Zero as his successor as concierge. Though initially detained, he is released by Henckels. However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. He is remembered as a refined hotelier, a philosophical and nihilistic character, and a man deeply moved by a pastry from Mendl's.

[ZERO]

Zero is a refugee from Aq Salim al-Jabat, having fled a war that destroyed his family and village, rendering him stateless and requiring a Special Transit Permit and a Migratory Visa with Stage Three Worker Status. He is deeply in love with Agatha, his girlfriend, to whom he proposes marriage and gives a book. He is protective and jealous of her, and works at Mendl's, often driving their delivery truck and carrying pastry boxes.

Throughout his adventures, Zero acts as M. Gustave's personal valet, accomplice, protégé, and trusted companion. He accompanies M. Gustave on numerous journeys and escapades, observing events, following instructions from monks, and assisting with various tasks, from navigating churches to preparing for travel. He is sworn to secrecy about The Society of the Crossed Keys. Zero plays a crucial role in the theft of the "Boy with Apple" painting, agreeing to a blood-pact with M. Gustave to sell it. He is instrumental in saving M. Gustave from Jopling, helping him escape Henckels' troops, and suggesting their escape plan to the Maltese Riviera.

Zero discovers Serge's murdered body, chases Jopling on a sled with M. Gustave, and retaliates against Dmitri when M. Gustave is attacked. He is arrested and injured during M. [BOY WITH APPLE]
Description: "BOY WITH APPLE" is a priceless and very valuable Flemish painting, estimated at five million Klubecks. This exquisite masterpiece by Johannes van Hoytl depicts a pale, young boy holding a piece of golden fruit. Considered one of the last van Hoytl paintings in private hands, it is a central object of contention in the will dispute of Madame D, who bequeathed it to M. Gustave.

The painting is a key element of the plot, becoming the subject of a theft. M. Gustave, believing it to be his rightful inheritance, takes the painting with the assistance of Zero, who suggests they "take it back." Dmitri Desgoffe und Taxis actively seeks the painting, and M. Gustave is implicated in its removal. M. Gustave and Zero plan to sell the stolen artwork, which is later discovered to have a hidden envelope on its reverse.

Beyond its role as a valuable art piece, "BOY WITH APPLE" is also an iconic image, featured on the cover of the menu in the Grand Budapest's dining room. While primarily described as a painting, it is also referred to as an artwork or image, and was once located on the wall behind M. Jean's desk. Although one description refers to it as a faded, old photograph or artwork, the overwhelming evidence points to it being a significant painting.

[AGATHA]
Description: Agatha is a central character, introduced as Zero's girlfriend and later his wife, for whom Zero (Mr. Moustafa) keeps the Grand Budapest Hotel, wearing her crossed-keys pendant as a symbol of their connection. She works at Mendl's pâtisserie as a highly skilled pastry chef, known for her expertise with a palette knife and butter-cream flourish, making and delivering beautifully-decorated pastries from Herr Mendl to the Executive Staff. She is described as cautious, observant, and brave, though she can be frightened, such as during an arrest by soldiers while traveling with M. Gustave and Zero. She is also depicted reading romantic poetry.

Her role in the unfolding events is crucial. Agatha is informed about the stolen "Boy with Apple" painting and given a coded message for her survival. She is seen running away, carrying a wrapped painting, and is pursued by Dmitri Desgoffe und Taxis through the hotel lobby and into an elevator, while simultaneously being sought by M. Gustave and Zero. During her efforts, she attempts to escape through a skylight from a building in a sleeping village, interacts with a soldier, finds a brass key, unlocks a vault, and retrieves the wrapped painting, noticing a detail on its back. She falls with Zero into a Mendl's van during their escape and receives a sliver of paper from him.

[VAULT]
Description: A secure storage pantry within the Grand Budapest Hotel, containing a combination lock, where Agatha retrieves a wrapped painting.

[DMITRI]
Description: Dmitri, also known as Mr. Desgoffe und Taxis, is Madame D's thirty-five-year-old son, and implicitly, Céline's son. He is a central figure in the dispute over his mother's will, initially expecting to inherit the bulk of her estate. Dmitri is described as ruthless and cold-blooded.

=== ENTITIES ===

[M. GUSTAVE]
Description: M. Gustave is a central and complex character, primarily known as the meticulous, liberally perfumed, and charming head concierge of the Grand Budapest Hotel in Nebelsbad. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

His life takes a dramatic turn following Madame D.'s death, which deeply affects him. He becomes embroiled in a dispute over her will, specifically concerning the valuable "Boy with Apple" painting, which he is bequeathed and later becomes the current owner of. Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

During his ordeal, M. Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. He is seen distributing food, including Mendl's pastries, to convicts, earning their trust as a "straight fella." After escaping with Zero's assistance, he is left without a safe house and plans to use disguises, aiming to escape to the Maltese Riviera and retrieve the "Boy with Apple."

M. Gustave is eventually cleared of the murder charges, having an alibi involving the Duke of Westfalia's wife. He continues his adventures with Zero, discovering a strangled person, chasing Jopling on a sled, and being saved by Zero from Jopling's attempts to leave him dangling from a cliff. He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

Later, M. Gustave expresses profound disgust and sadness over the transformation of the Grand Budapest Hotel into a "troop's barracks." He interviews Agatha, flirts with her, and approves of her union with Zero. Ultimately, M. Gustave anoints Zero as his successor as concierge. Though initially detained, he is released by Henckels. However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. === ENTITIES ===

[M. GUSTAVE]
Description: M. Gustave is a central and complex character, primarily known as the meticulous, liberally perfumed, and charming head concierge of the Grand Budapest Hotel in Nebelsbad. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

His life takes a dramatic turn following Madame D.'s death, which deeply affects him. He becomes embroiled in a dispute over her will, specifically concerning the valuable "Boy with Apple" painting, which he is bequeathed and later becomes the current owner of. Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

During his ordeal, M. Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. He is seen distributing food, including Mendl's pastries, to convicts, earning their trust as a "straight fella." After escaping with Zero's assistance, he is left without a safe house and plans to use disguises, aiming to escape to the Maltese Riviera and retrieve the "Boy with Apple."

M. Gustave is eventually cleared of the murder charges, having an alibi involving the Duke of Westfalia's wife. He continues his adventures with Zero, discovering a strangled person, chasing Jopling on a sled, and being saved by Zero from Jopling's attempts to leave him dangling from a cliff. He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

Later, M. Gustave expresses profound disgust and sadness over the transformation of the Grand Budapest Hotel into a "troop's barracks." He interviews Agatha, flirts with her, and approves of her union with Zero. Ultimately, M. Gustave anoints Zero as his successor as concierge. Though initially detained, he is released by Henckels. However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. He is remembered as a refined hotelier, a philosophical and nihilistic character, and a man deeply moved by a pastry from Mendl's.

[GRAND BUDAPEST HOTEL]
Description: The Grand Budapest Hotel is a prestigious, five-star institution located in Nebelsbad, serving as the central setting where many of the story's events unfold. In its prime, M. Gustave held the esteemed position of head concierge and manager, while Zero Moustafa (also known as Mr. Moustafa) began his career there as a Junior Lobby Boy. The hotel was known for its distinctive stationery, which featured a unique crossed keys insignia.

[BOY WITH APPLE]
Description: "BOY WITH APPLE" is a priceless and very valuable Flemish painting, estimated at five million Klubecks. This exquisite masterpiece by Johannes van Hoytl depicts a pale, young boy holding a piece of golden fruit. Considered one of the last van Hoytl paintings in private hands, it is a central object of contention in the will dispute of Madame D, who bequeathed it to M. Gustave.

The painting is a key element of the plot, becoming the subject of a theft. M. Gustave, believing it to be his rightful inheritance, takes the painting with the assistance of Zero, who suggests they "take it back." Dmitri Desgoffe und Taxis actively seeks the painting, and M. Gustave is implicated in its removal. M. Gustave and Zero plan to sell the stolen artwork, which is later discovered to have a hidden envelope on its reverse.

Beyond its role as a valuable art piece, "BOY WITH APPLE" is also an iconic image, featured on the cover of the menu in the Grand Budapest's dining room. While primarily described as a painting, it is also referred to as an artwork or image, and was once located on the wall behind M. Jean's desk. Although one description refers to it as a faded, old photograph or artwork, the overwhelming evidence points to it being a significant painting.

Description: No description available

Description: The act of killing someone, which was the contingency for Madame D's second will, and the cause of death for Serge's sister and Serge himself.

[SECOND WILL]
Description: A legal document created by Madame D, to be executed only in the event of her death by murder, a copy of which Serge pulled.

[M. GUSTAVE]
Description: M. Gustave is a central and complex character, primarily known as the meticulous, liberally perfumed, and charming head concierge of the Grand Budapest Hotel in Nebelsbad. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

His life takes a dramatic turn following Madame D.'s death, which deeply affects him. He becomes embroiled in a dispute over her will, specifically concerning the valuable "Boy with Apple" painting, which he is bequeathed and later becomes the current owner of. Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

During his ordeal, M. Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. He is seen distributing food, including Mendl's pastries, to convicts, earning their trust as a "straight fella." After escaping with Zero's assistance, he is left without a safe house and plans to use disguises, aiming to escape to the Maltese Riviera and retrieve the "Boy with Apple."

M. Gustave is eventually cleared of the murder charges, having an alibi involving the Duke of Westfalia's wife. He continues his adventures with Zero, discovering a strangled person, chasing Jopling on a sled, and being saved by Zero from Jopling's attempts to leave him dangling from a cliff. He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

Later, M. Gustave expresses profound disgust and sadness over the transformation of the Grand Budapest Hotel into a "troop's barracks." He interviews Agatha, flirts with her, and approves of her union with Zero. Ultimately, M. Gustave anoints Zero as his successor as concierge. Though initially detained, he is released by Henckels. However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. He is remembered as a refined hotelier, a philosophical and nihilistic character, and a man deeply moved by a pastry from Mendl's.

- CÉLINE'S WILL --[M. Gustave is involved in a dispute over Céline's will, particularly regarding the "Boy with Apple" painting.]--> M. GUSTAVE

Description: M. Gustave is a central and complex character, primarily known as the meticulous, liberally perfumed, and charming head concierge of the Grand Budapest Hotel in Nebelsbad. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

His life takes a dramatic turn following Madame D.'s death, which deeply affects him. He becomes embroiled in a dispute over her will, specifically concerning the valuable "Boy with Apple" painting, which he is bequeathed and later becomes the current owner of. Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

During his ordeal, M. Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. He is seen distributing food, including Mendl's pastries, to convicts, earning their trust as a "straight fella." After escaping with Zero's assistance, he is left without a safe house and plans to use disguises, aiming to escape to the Maltese Riviera and retrieve the "Boy with Apple."

M. Gustave is eventually cleared of the murder charges, having an alibi involving the Duke of Westfalia's wife. He continues his adventures with Zero, discovering a strangled person, chasing Jopling on a sled, and being saved by Zero from Jopling's attempts to leave him dangling from a cliff. He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

Later, M. Gustave expresses profound disgust and sadness over the transformation of the Grand Budapest Hotel into a "troop's barracks." He interviews Agatha, flirts with her, and approves of her union with Zero. Ultimately, M. Gustave anoints Zero as his successor as concierge. Though initially detained, he is released by Henckels. However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. He is remembered as a refined hotelier, a philosophical and nihilistic character, and a man deeply moved by a pastry from Mendl's.

=== ENTITIES ===

[M. GUSTAVE]
Description: M. Gustave is a central and complex character, primarily known as the meticulous, liberally perfumed, and charming head concierge of the Grand Budapest Hotel in Nebelsbad. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

His life takes a dramatic turn following Madame D.'s death, which deeply affects him. He becomes embroiled in a dispute over her will, specifically concerning the valuable "Boy with Apple" painting, which he is bequeathed and later becomes the current owner of. Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

During his ordeal, M. Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. He is seen distributing food, including Mendl's pastries, to convicts, earning their trust as a "straight fella." After escaping with Zero's assistance, he is left without a safe house and plans to use disguises, aiming to escape to the Maltese Riviera and retrieve the "Boy with Apple."

M. Gustave is eventually cleared of the murder charges, having an alibi involving the Duke of Westfalia's wife. He continues his adventures with Zero, discovering a strangled person, chasing Jopling on a sled, and being saved by Zero from Jopling's attempts to leave him dangling from a cliff. He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

Later, M. Gustave expresses profound disgust and sadness over the transformation of the Grand Budapest Hotel into a "troop's barracks." He interviews Agatha, flirts with her, and approves of her union with Zero. Ultimately, M. Gustave anoints Zero as his successor as concierge. Though initially detained, he is released by Henckels. However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. He is remembered as a refined hotelier, a philosophical and nihilistic character, and a man deeply moved by a pastry from Mendl's.

[MADAME D]
Description: Madame D is a deceased, distinguished, and wealthy individual, identified as the Dowager Countess. Her death, reported in the Trans-Alpine Yodel, is a central plot point and is linked to a murder case. Her Last Will and Testament, detailing the distribution of her vast estate, is of significant importance. Her will is mentioned and examined by Dmitri, and a second will, created in the event of her murder, is revealed by Serge. The discussion surrounding her will also takes place in Deputy Kovacs's office. Madame D was a guest of the Grand Budapest Hotel and had a close relationship with M. Gustave, who is deeply grieved by her passing. She left him a letter and a significant sum of money.

[MADAME D.]
Description: MADAME D., also known as Mdm. C.V.D.u.T., was an immaculately-dressed, eighty-year-old woman. During her stay as a guest at the Grand Budapest, she displayed significant frustration, weeping, and anxiety concerning travel, expressing both fear and reluctance to depart. She engaged in prayer and shared a deep affection for M. Gustave, who, at one point, criticized her nail polish. Before her departure, she gave M. Gustave a five Klubeck coin, asking him to light a candle for her at Santa Maria.

Tragically, MADAME D. was later found deceased, referred to as "the dead widow," having died from strychnine poisoning in her private chambers at the Desgoffe und Taxis Residence. Her murder led to M. Gustave being accused, and he subsequently visited her corpse. At the time of her death, her fingernails were lacquered in plum. Her estate included a mansion located in Lutz, and her "Last Will and Testament" was presented by Deputy Kovacs, who served as the executor of her estate.

=== ENTITIES ===

[M. GUSTAVE]
Description: M. Gustave is a central and complex character, primarily known as the meticulous, liberally perfumed, and charming head concierge of the Grand Budapest Hotel in Nebelsbad. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

His life takes a dramatic turn following Madame D.'s death, which deeply affects him. He becomes embroiled in a dispute over her will, specifically concerning the valuable "Boy with Apple" painting, which he is bequeathed and later becomes the current owner of. Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

During his ordeal, M. Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. He is seen distributing food, including Mendl's pastries, to convicts, earning their trust as a "straight fella." After escaping with Zero's assistance, he is left without a safe house and plans to use disguises, aiming to escape to the Maltese Riviera and retrieve the "Boy with Apple."

M. Gustave is eventually cleared of the murder charges, having an alibi involving the Duke of Westfalia's wife. He continues his adventures with Zero, discovering a strangled person, chasing Jopling on a sled, and being saved by Zero from Jopling's attempts to leave him dangling from a cliff. He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

Later, M. Gustave expresses profound disgust and sadness over the transformation of the Grand Budapest Hotel into a "troop's barracks." He interviews Agatha, flirts with her, and approves of her union with Zero. Ultimately, M. Gustave anoints Zero as his successor as concierge. Though initially detained, he is released by Henckels. However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. He is remembered as a refined hotelier, a philosophical and nihilistic character, and a man deeply moved by a pastry from Mendl's.

He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. === ENTITIES ===

[ARREST OF M. GUSTAVE AND ZERO]

[PRISON]
Description: A correctional facility that M. Gustave dreads returning to.

[ZERO]
Description: "ZERO" is introduced as a Junior Lobby Boy in training at the Grand Budapest Hotel, who quickly becomes the devoted pupil, counselor, and guardian of M. Gustave. He is later known as Mr. Moustafa, and ultimately becomes M. Gustave's sole heir and successor at the Grand Budapest Hotel, also serving as the narrator (Mr. Moustafa V.O.).

Zero is a refugee from Aq Salim al-Jabat, having fled a war that destroyed his family and village, rendering him stateless and requiring a Special Transit Permit and a Migratory Visa with Stage Three Worker Status. He is deeply in love with Agatha, his girlfriend, to whom he proposes marriage and gives a book. He is protective and jealous of her, and works at Mendl's, often driving their delivery truck and carrying pastry boxes.

Throughout his adventures, Zero acts as M. Gustave's personal valet, accomplice, protégé, and trusted companion. He accompanies M. Gustave on numerous journeys and escapades, observing events, following instructions from monks, and assisting with various tasks, from navigating churches to preparing for travel. He is sworn to secrecy about The Society of the Crossed Keys. Zero plays a crucial role in the theft of the "Boy with Apple" painting, agreeing to a blood-pact with M. Gustave to sell it. He is instrumental in saving M. Gustave from Jopling, helping him escape Henckels' troops, and suggesting their escape plan to the Maltese Riviera.

Zero discovers Serge's murdered body, chases Jopling on a sled with M. Gustave, and retaliates against Dmitri when M. Gustave is attacked. He is arrested and injured during M. Gustave's detention but is later released by Henckels. He is questioned by authorities and visits M. Gustave in prison. Zero is also depicted as agile, capable of shimmying up skylights and running across roofs to communicate with Agatha. He is concerned for M. Gustave, discussing his legal situation and bringing him treats.

As Mr. Moustafa, he trains the new Lobby Boy, Otto, and expresses alarm and shared sentiments about the hotel's declining state. He is a trusted staff member who reads M. Gustave's letters to the assembled staff. Zero's journey culminates in him finding and embracing Agatha, solidifying his personal happiness before his eventual succession to M. Gustave's legacy.

[M. GUSTAVE]
Description: M. Gustave is a central and complex character, primarily known as the meticulous, liberally perfumed, and charming head concierge of the Grand Budapest Hotel in Nebelsbad. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

His life takes a dramatic turn following Madame D.'s death, which deeply affects him. He becomes embroiled in a dispute over her will, specifically concerning the valuable "Boy with Apple" painting, which he is bequeathed and later becomes the current owner of. Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

During his ordeal, M. Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. He is seen distributing food, including Mendl's pastries, to convicts, earning their trust as a "straight fella." After escaping with Zero's assistance, he is left without a safe house and plans to use disguises, aiming to escape to the Maltese Riviera and retrieve the "Boy with Apple."

M. Gustave is eventually cleared of the murder charges, having an alibi involving the Duke of Westfalia's wife. He continues his adventures with Zero, discovering a strangled person, chasing Jopling on a sled, and being saved by Zero from Jopling's attempts to leave him dangling from a cliff. He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

Later, M. Gustave expresses profound disgust and sadness over the transformation of the Grand Budapest Hotel into a "troop's barracks." He interviews Agatha, flirts with her, and approves of her union with Zero. Ultimately, M. Gustave anoints Zero as his successor as concierge. Though initially detained, he is released by Henckels. However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. He is remembered as a refined hotelier, a philosophical and nihilistic character, and a man deeply moved by a pastry from Mendl's.

[BOY WITH APPLE]
Description: "BOY WITH APPLE" is a priceless and very valuable Flemish painting, estimated at five million Klubecks. This exquisite masterpiece by Johannes van Hoytl depicts a pale, young boy holding a piece of golden fruit. Considered one of the last van Hoytl paintings in private hands, it is a central object of contention in the will dispute of Madame D, who bequeathed it to M. Gustave.

The painting is a key element of the plot, becoming the subject of a theft. M. Gustave, believing it to be his rightful inheritance, takes the painting with the assistance of Zero, who suggests they "take it back." Dmitri Desgoffe und Taxis actively seeks the painting, and M. Gustave is implicated in its removal. M. Gustave and Zero plan to sell the stolen artwork, which is later discovered to have a hidden envelope on its reverse.

Beyond its role as a valuable art piece, "BOY WITH APPLE" is also an iconic image, featured on the cover of the menu in the Grand Budapest's dining room. While primarily described as a painting, it is also referred to as an artwork or image, and was once located on the wall behind M. Jean's desk. Although one description refers to it as a faded, old photograph or artwork, the overwhelming evidence points to it being a significant painting.

[GRAND BUDAPEST HOTEL]
Description: The Grand Budapest Hotel is a prestigious, five-star institution located in Nebelsbad, serving as the central setting where many of the story's events unfold. In its prime, M. Gustave held the esteemed position of head concierge and manager, while Zero Moustafa (also known as Mr. Moustafa) began his career there as a Junior Lobby Boy. The hotel was known for its distinctive stationery, which featured a unique crossed keys insignia.

He later appointed Zero as his successor, both in his role as concierge and as the eventual owner. Over time, the property underwent changes, becoming "common property" before it was ultimately acquired by Zero Moustafa. By this later period, the Grand Budapest Hotel was described as an "enchanting, old ruin," a stark contrast to its earlier grandeur.

=== ENTITIES ===

[SHED]
Description: A small structure across the courtyard from which Jopling emerges on skis.

[SKI LOCKER]
Description: A designated storage area within the shed, marked by a sign "Clerical Use Only", from which Jopling likely obtained his skis.

[FAMILY DESGOFFE UND TAXIS]
Description: The employer of Jopling, whose mother was one of the victims mentioned by a shifty guard.

[JOPLING]
Description: Jopling is a ruthless, cold-blooded, and stony character who serves as a private inquiry agent employed by the wealthy Desgoffe und Taxis family. He often acts as an enforcer and henchman for Dmitri, accompanying him, acting as his thug with brass knuckles, and even restraining him at times. Jopling is present during discussions about the family inheritance and follows Dmitri out the door.

Jopling is a dangerous individual, known to carry various concealed weapons. He rides a black motorcycle, which he uses to follow Deputy Kovacs to the Kunstmuseum Lutz. He is strongly implied to be the one who brutally attacked Deputy Kovacs, severing his fingers, collecting them, and walking away. Jopling is aware of Deputy Vilmos Kovacs' disappearance and is actively searching for Serge X.

His activities include stopping at a gas station, where he is seen reading a torn radio telegram, and waiting on the threshold of a cottage to hand a woman his card. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. Description: M. Gustave is a central and complex character, primarily known as the meticulous, liberally perfumed, and charming head concierge of the Grand Budapest Hotel in Nebelsbad. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

His life takes a dramatic turn following Madame D.'s death, which deeply affects him. He becomes embroiled in a dispute over her will, specifically concerning the valuable "Boy with Apple" painting, which he is bequeathed and later becomes the current owner of. Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

During his ordeal, M. Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. He is seen distributing food, including Mendl's pastries, to convicts, earning their trust as a "straight fella." After escaping with Zero's assistance, he is left without a safe house and plans to use disguises, aiming to escape to the Maltese Riviera and retrieve the "Boy with Apple."

M. Gustave is eventually cleared of the murder charges, having an alibi involving the Duke of Westfalia's wife. He continues his adventures with Zero, discovering a strangled person, chasing Jopling on a sled, and being saved by Zero from Jopling's attempts to leave him dangling from a cliff. He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

Later, M. Gustave expresses profound disgust and sadness over the transformation of the Grand Budapest Hotel into a "troop's barracks." He interviews Agatha, flirts with her, and approves of her union with Zero. Ultimately, M. Gustave anoints Zero as his successor as concierge. Though initially detained, he is released by Henckels. However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. He is remembered as a refined hotelier, a philosophical and nihilistic character, and a man deeply moved by a pastry from Mendl's.

She engaged in prayer and shared a deep affection for M. Gustave, who, at one point, criticized her nail polish. Before her departure, she gave M. Gustave a five Klubeck coin, asking him to light a candle for her at Santa Maria.

Her murder led to M. Gustave being accused, and he subsequently visited her corpse. At the time of her death, her fingernails were lacquered in plum. Her estate included a mansion located in Lutz, and her "Last Will and Testament" was presented by Deputy Kovacs, who served as the executor of her estate.

Her will is mentioned and examined by Dmitri, and a second will, created in the event of her murder, is revealed by Serge. The discussion surrounding her will also takes place in Deputy Kovacs's office. Madame D was a guest of the Grand Budapest Hotel and had a close relationship with M. [M. GUSTAVE]
Description: M. Gustave is a central and complex character, primarily known as the meticulous, liberally perfumed, and charming head concierge of the Grand Budapest Hotel in Nebelsbad. Described as a tall, blond, forty-year-old man, he is renowned for his composure and attentiveness, delivering nightly sermons to his staff and maintaining intimate relationships with several wealthy, elderly female guests, most notably Madame D. He expresses deep love and pride in Madame D.'s loyalty, attempting to soothe her, dry her tears, and even criticizing her nail polish while reciting poetry to calm her.

M. Gustave serves as a mentor and friend to Zero, a Lobby Boy at the Grand Budapest, with whom he travels extensively. He highly values L'air de Panache, a perfume he receives from M. Ivan, and expresses deep regret for any harsh words he may have directed at Zero. He is also a business manager who meets with Herr Becker and is irritated by Zero's interruptions.

His life takes a dramatic turn following Madame D.'s death, which deeply affects him. He becomes embroiled in a dispute over her will, specifically concerning the valuable "Boy with Apple" painting, which he is bequeathed and later becomes the current owner of. Accused of Madame D.'s murder, M. Gustave claims innocence, seeks to clear his name, and possesses "Grand Budapest pass-keys." He is pursued as a "fugitive from justice" by Henckels, whom he knew as a child, and is physically assaulted by Dmitri.

During his ordeal, M. Gustave is arrested and jailed, where he works diligently with fellow convicts like Ludwig, Pinky, Günther, and Wolf, planning and executing an elaborate escape from a prison-castle. He is seen distributing food, including Mendl's pastries, to convicts, earning their trust as a "straight fella." After escaping with Zero's assistance, he is left without a safe house and plans to use disguises, aiming to escape to the Maltese Riviera and retrieve the "Boy with Apple."

M. Gustave is eventually cleared of the murder charges, having an alibi involving the Duke of Westfalia's wife. He continues his adventures with Zero, discovering a strangled person, chasing Jopling on a sled, and being saved by Zero from Jopling's attempts to leave him dangling from a cliff. He is also involved in a plot concerning missing persons and a stolen item, calling upon the special services of The Society of the Crossed Keys.

Later, M. Gustave expresses profound disgust and sadness over the transformation of the Grand Budapest Hotel into a "troop's barracks." He interviews Agatha, flirts with her, and approves of her union with Zero. Ultimately, M. Gustave anoints Zero as his successor as concierge. Though initially detained, he is released by Henckels. However, his journey concludes tragically when he is arrested and later shot by soldiers in black uniforms, a fate that occurs after his exoneration from the murder charge. He is remembered as a refined hotelier, a philosophical and nihilistic character, and a man deeply moved by a pastry from Mendl's.

He is deeply in love with Agatha, his girlfriend, to whom he proposes marriage and gives a book. He is protective and jealous of her, and works at Mendl's, often driving their delivery truck and carrying pastry boxes.

Gustave on numerous journeys and escapades, observing events, following instructions from monks, and assisting with various tasks, from navigating churches to preparing for travel. He is sworn to secrecy about The Society of the Crossed Keys. Zero plays a crucial role in the theft of the "Boy with Apple" painting, agreeing to a blood-pact with M. Gustave to sell it. He is instrumental in saving M. Gustave from Jopling, helping him escape Henckels' troops, and suggesting their escape plan to the Maltese Riviera.

Gustave's detention but is later released by Henckels. He is questioned by authorities and visits M. Gustave in prison. Gustave, discussing his legal situation and bringing him treats.

Gustave's letters to the assembled staff. Zero's journey culminates in him finding and embracing Agatha, solidifying his personal happiness before his eventual succession to M. Gustave's legacy.

Description: Jopling is a ruthless, cold-blooded, and stony character who serves as a private inquiry agent employed by the wealthy Desgoffe und Taxis family. He often acts as an enforcer and henchman for Dmitri, accompanying him, acting as his thug with brass knuckles, and even restraining him at times. Jopling is present during discussions about the family inheritance and follows Dmitri out the door.

Jopling is a dangerous individual, known to carry various concealed weapons. He rides a black motorcycle, which he uses to follow Deputy Kovacs to the Kunstmuseum Lutz. He is strongly implied to be the one who brutally attacked Deputy Kovacs, severing his fingers, collecting them, and walking away. Jopling is aware of Deputy Vilmos Kovacs' disappearance and is actively searching for Serge X.

His activities include stopping at a gas station, where he is seen reading a torn radio telegram, and waiting on the threshold of a cottage to hand a woman his card. He is also observed reading a newspaper in an office building lobby and is present in Deputy Kovacs's office, where he is seen stroking a Siamese cat. Jopling is also a civilian personnel present at a cellblock during a military investigation.

Jopling is a persistent antagonist, pursuing M. Gustave and Zero on skis. He attempts to kill M. Gustave by stomping on the ice M. Gustave is clinging to, but is ultimately pushed off a cliff by Zero. He also attacks Zero after Zero punches Dmitri.

Description: Serge X is a young man who is currently reported missing. He is employed in the service of the Desgoffe und Taxis family, and Jopling is actively searching for him. Serge X also has a sister, who works as a washer-woman.

=== ENTITIES ===
